Eddie Short ran our final lap of about 3 miles, and although he caught Butler, of Surrey A.C., he was eventually beaten on the final run-in by about a yard.

Eddie Short was running for the R.A.F. in a match against the U.A.U. and Midland Counties, and Bob Taylor, who was indisposed. In mentioning the above names we are not attempting to detract from Jack Brown's running in winning the race, as his time was well up to standard and he finished in comforta…
Jack Brown, John Bromley, Archie Bedford and Eddie Short were notable absentees, and the first three named were included in our Brighton team, with Eddie as 1st reserve.
Also in the 1 mile team race we only had the Bishop brothers, plus Eddie Short, and although Eddie was 5th, our other runners brought up the rear and so we were placed 5th.
At the bell Ross jumped away from John, who seemed suddenly to "crack," with the result that he was passed for 2nd place, and Eddie Short almost caught him down the straight for 3rd position.
We had no runners in the 2 mile steeplechase, as John Bromley elected to run in the 2 miles flat and Eddie Short could not get away from Camp in time.

We had two runners in the 2 mile steeplechase in John Bromley and Eddie Short, and in the early stages John was running well in 4th place. He came a cropper at the water-jump and was carried off with a damaged ankle, which was certainly very bad luck, and we trust he will soon recover from his injury.
Near the end of the winter season, Eddie Short was in hospital suffering from a kick in the back, sustained while playing for the camp Rugby team, and who should be in the same R.A.F. ward but E.

Chas Walker dropped a place on the long 7th relay but Len Bishop who ran very well, took us back into 2nd place on the 8th leg.Eddie Short and Bob Taylor maintained this position on the two final stages and were unable to overtake the leaders Essex Beagles, who returned a time of 3 hours 49 mins,16secs. to our 3.50.33.

This event which carries with it the Macher Shield was held on January 30th and the holder Jack Brown, made sure of retaining the trophy by scoring a runaway victory in the fast time of 55mins. 9secs. Chas.Walker 55.02 was 2nd with Jim Masters 3rd in 55.17, the next three placings being P.Bagnall 55…
Stearman 65th and E. Short 72nd place which was only good enough to put us in 6th position.

Bedford,our junior D.Baulch,L.Herbert Bill Lucas, Dennis Brickwood, Len Bishop, Eddie Short, S. Gawler and Mike Stearman all of whom were to give the selectors some head aches when trying to find the best team for the approaching National Brighton Relay.

Our next two home were Stan Gawler 98th, and Eddie Short 128th.Both these runners were further back than expected, although in fairness to Eddie Short it must be stated that his training has been interrupted this winter.

We had a competitor in each event except the pole vault which certainly shows the growth of the section. Eddie Short was 3rd in the 3000 metres steeplechase. I am now looking forward to the Kinnaird and hope we shall again make a good show.
Eddie Short was very unlucky in the steeplechase. He was lying second when he twisted his foot at the water jump with two laps to go and had to retire.

Our new Cross Country Captain, Eddie Short, then took over at Purley for the long grind to Earlswood and I suppose no one could wish for a less envious task than to chase Alec Olney of T.V.H. who must be considered one of the best road runners of all time.
We were well back on the first leg, but were brought from 9th to 2nd during the next two legs. Len Herbert maintained this but Eddie Short lost a place which John Bromley was unable to regain.
The lecture on "Body levers" was most interesting and I know Eddie Short was most enthusiastic about it. The "Weight" training session was again most enlightening.
Eddie Short continued his "come back" training to come in 3rd ahead of Charlie Smart. Our sole representative in the Junior events was Archie Boreham who gained 3rd place in his 880.
Jack Brown is to be congratulated on once again getting his name inscribed on the trophy as also are Eddie Short and George Davidson on their 2nd and 3rd placings.

Behind Dave we had a rather large gap, but nevertheless the team were well backed up by Eric Gebbett and Eddie Short. The team showed up well by finishing 7th out of 50 clubs who actually closed in a team.
Next came Eric Bishop closely followed by Alan and somewhere in the forties Eddie Short and Brian Trower side by side. Bob Plummer was about 100th followed by Wally Wortley and Charlie Manning.
Eddie Short did excellently to take fourth place in the steeplechase in a good class field. Percy Luxon was 2nd in the Long Jump and Ash with a 6 foot jump was third in the high.

Our two steeplechasers Eddie Short and Pete Baganll, finished 3rd and 5th after taking a horrible bashing in the process. It is a pity that some of our longer distance track men don't display courage of this sort and help Belgrave to once again take its place at the front in distance running.

Although still very husky from a heavy cold, Shippen was about the 100 mark with Len Bishop, Eddie Short and Jim Heathfield further back. And so it was, our lads hung on grimly to their early gains and ran out a good third with Jack Brown, a little disappointed perhaps, our first man home.
Eddie Short who had taken fourth place in the Steeplechase last year, ran again. He said that he was not so fit as last year but was running gamely.

The juniors ran in the same race and Charlie Dabbs and Robin Weate followed Archie round, closely pursued by Eddie Short and Clive Shippen. The brothers Bishop (Alan and Eric) indulged in some good pack running with Jim Heathfield and Bob Glover in attendance.
Len Bishop and Eddie Short should have been at least ten places higher than their 42nd and 43rd, and Peter Hitchcock should also have been better positioned than 52nd.
Eddie Short ran well to take sixth place and that "little potterer" Joe Dooley followed close on his heels with Jim Heathfield, only a few yards behind.
Then followed a string of runners before we again saw a Belgrave vest filled by Eddie Short who had John Moore and Jumbo Masters close on his heels, all of them in the 130's.

John Moore and Eddie Short soon discovered their mistake and all was well once more but the whole character of the race had been changed. Nevertheless we gained a comfortable win, scoring seven a side, with 46 points against 82 by Finchley and 103 by Orpington.

Our two entries in the 3000 metres steeplechase, although not placed, performed most creditably, both beating time standard of 10m.15s; Clive Shippen finishing in 10m.3.6s. and Eddie Short in 10m.12s.
Eddie Short, running for the 'C' remained in 13th place but Dennis Jones dropped the 'D' back to 14th. The 'E' team had shot its bolt and had no runners on this stage.

Newcomers to the team were Tom Clinton, Ken Stimpson, Martin Williamson and Eddie Short. Twenty-five clubs competed in 1949 and we accomplished our second hat-trick of wins, thus achieving more wins in the nineteen races held than any other club.
Walker 50th, Eddie Short 55th and Mal Robinson way back 67th. A further gap followed before Dennis Jones appeared 83rd, John Collier 90th and Mike Stearman 92nd.

In the Surrey Bill Lucas won the 3 miles with 3rd places in the mile by Charlie Walker, the steeplechase by Eddie Short and in both sprints by Bas.
Eddie Short ran well against Birchfield's ace Freddie Green and finally Jack Brown took us to within 5 seconds of winning the event on that last stage with his Club Record breaking run.
In the Junior race Eddie Short was again our first man home in 7th position, and to gain such a high place in this race speaks well for Eddie's strength and determination.

In the Junior race Eddie Short again ran well ... he was our first man home in 13th place. C.W.Walker, the winner of our recent road race for Novices, did well in his first “open” race to finish in 34th position, but we missed the services of Arthur Bruce, who could not get leave from his unit.

We are sorry to record the death last November of Eddie Short, a regular in our running teams after the war. Eddie served in the RAF where he also played rugby but he got away from camp as often as possible to race for the Bels.

We heard with sadness during the year of the deaths of Charlie Jones, Frank Jarvis and Win Shepherd, who were Presidents of the Club in 1959/60,1966/67 and 1990/91 respectively, and also of Don Brown, Daye Donovan, Len Herbert and Eddie Short.
